title: Remediate transitive FFI crypto vulnerability and introduce runtime crypto policy
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: A transitive dependency (libffi bindings used by the legacy SSO XML adapter) surfaced a potential memory-corruption vector when combined with an older OpenSSL bonding layer. This ticket covers triage, a short-term mitigation, and a medium-term remediation that upgrades affected libraries and introduces a runtime-level crypto policy that standardizes acceptable ciphers, key sizes, and validation behavior across services.
comments: 2025-02-12 - triage: Security pager flagged an abnormal mem access pattern in service-auth during SSO assertion parsing. Reproducer attached in Confluence. Initial scope: services using legacy-sso-adapter and the python ffi binding chain (pyffi -> cffi -> libffi).

2025-02-13 - analysis: Root cause appears only when libffi is combined with OpenSSL <=1.1.1 backported shims. Not all codepaths reproduce; deterministic in unit harness with crafted SAML assertion. Proof-of-concept created by @Evelyn Park. Low-confidence exploit surface but unacceptable for enterprise customers.

2025-02-15 - mitigation: Feature-flagged 'sso.strict_assertion_parsing' and deployed soft-fail mode to prod (reject but log instead of crashing). Also added runtime gating to disable ffi-backed adapters until patched. This reduced incident noise while we prepare the patch. Rollback plan in place if new regressions appear.

2025-02-20 - plan: Two-track remediation: (1) Upgrade transitive FFI bindings and OpenSSL shim to latest patched builds and backport tests; (2) Implement a runtime 'crypto-policy' that centralizes rules: min TLS version 1.3, disallow RSA<2048, require JWK kid pinning for assertion keys, prefer Ed25519/ECDSA-P256, and disable legacy ciphers. Crypto-policy will be exposed as a service-level config with a canary rollout.

2025-02-25 - implementation: Created experimental runtime flag runtime.crypto_policy=v1.0 and local test harness. Implemented validation hooks in auth service to consult centralized policy before accepting keys. Benchmarked token verification latency: +0.8ms median per assertion when policy checks enabled (within SLO). Pull request created: PR #14258 (link above).

2025-03-01 - code review notes: Security review requested from @Marco Diaz and @Lena Sørensen. Requested changes: more granular feature-flagging for per-tenant strictness, explicit test coverage for malformed assertions, and an audit log event for policy rejections. Addressed comments and added property-based tests for assertion parser.

2025-03-03 - rollout: Canary deployed to 5% of traffic in us-west-2 under runtime-1.24 candidate. Observed no crashes and auth success rate steady. However, small spike in rejected assertions from an enterprise tenant using an older IdP; engineering contacted the customer success manager to coordinate key rotation/reconfig.

2025-03-04 - next steps: Merge PR after final security sign-off, add automated build-time scan to CI to detect vulnerable transitive FFI/OpenSSL combinations, schedule full rollout with 24h ramp and a post-deployment verification runbook. Prepare KB for affected customers and update SSO migration guide.
